newsitem.title: USA: Moslems say Virginia police harass them over veils.
newsitem.headline: Moslems say Virginia police harass them over veils.

text.p: Two Moslem women have accused policemen in Portsmouth, Virginia, of stopping and searching them because they wore face veils in public, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The women say the officers fondled them during the search and handcuffed them, the Virginian Pilot said. They have now filed a complaint against the police alleging sexual assault.
A Portsmouth police spokeswoman said she could not comment on the case.

The police officers considered the women's veils, part of the traditional Islamic hijab dress, to be masks, the newspaper said. Wearing masks in public is illegal in Virginia, a law stemming from efforts to combat the Ku Klux Klan white supremacy organisation.

The police stopped the women on Sunday night as they walked towards a shop in Portsmouth after prayers. One of the women explained she was wearing Islamic dress but she was told to remove the veil, the Pilot said. When they refused, they were handcuffed and searched.
They told the newspaper that officers fondled them during the search in the parking lot.
"I just kept saying 'Stop touching me,'" one was quoted as saying. "He was just touching me and fondling me all over."
The women were taken to a police station but released without charge.
